title: Multi-Omics Identification of Genetic Alterations in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Therapeutic Efficacy of HNC018 as a Novel Multi-Target Agent for c-MET/STAT3/AKT Signaling Axis.
authors: Khedkar, Harshita Nivrutti; Chen, Lung-Ching; Kuo, Yu-Cheng; Wu, Alexander T H; Huang, Hsu-Shan
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学与计算机辅助方法鉴定HNSCC中MET/STAT3/AKT靶点并评估小分子药物HNC018的疗效，虽涉及蛋白靶点结合，但核心是药物抗癌活性与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Amongst the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by high morbidity and mortality. The failure of standard treatment modalities, such as surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, demands the need for in-depth understanding of the complex signaling networks involved in the development of treatment resistance. A tumor's invasive growth and high levels of intrinsic or acquired treatment resistance are the primary causes of treatment failure. This may be a result of the presence of HNSCC's cancer stem cells, which are known to have self-renewing capabilities that result in therapeutic resistance. Using bioinformatics methods, we discovered that elevated expressions of MET, STAT3, and AKT were associated with poor overall survival in HNSCC patients. We then evaluated the therapeutic potential of our newly synthesized small molecule HNC018 towards its potential as a novel anticancer drug. Our computer-aided structure characterization and target identification study predicted that HNC018 could target these oncogenic markers implicated in HNSCC. Subsequently, the HNC018 has demonstrated its anti-proliferative and anticancer activities towards the head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell lines, along with displaying the stronger binding affinities towards the MET, STAT3, and AKT than the standard drug cisplatin. Reduction in the clonogenic and tumor-sphere-forming ability displays HNC018's role in decreasing the tumorigenicity. Importantly, an vivo study has shown a significant delay in tumor growth in HNC018 alone or in combination with cisplatin-treated xenograft mice model. Collectively with our findings, HNC018 highlights the desirable properties of a drug-like candidate and could be considered as a novel small molecule for treating head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract_zh: 在全球最常见的恶性肿瘤中，头颈部鳞状细胞癌（HNSCC）以高发病率和高死亡率为特征。手术、放疗和化疗等标准治疗手段的失败，要求深入理解涉及治疗耐药性发展的复杂信号网络。肿瘤的侵袭性生长及高水平的内在或获得性治疗耐药性是治疗失败的主要原因。这可能是由于HNSCC癌症干细胞的存在，这些细胞已知具有自我更新能力，从而导致治疗耐药性。通过生物信息学方法，我们发现MET、STAT3和AKT的高表达与HNSCC患者的总生存率较差相关。随后，我们评估了新合成的小分子HNC018作为新型抗癌药物的治疗潜力。我们的计算机辅助结构表征和靶点识别研究预测，HNC018可能靶向这些与HNSCC相关的致癌标志物。接着，HNC018在头颈部鳞状细胞癌细胞系中展示了其抗增殖和抗癌活性，并且与标准药物顺铂相比，对MET、STAT3和AKT显示出更强的结合亲和力。克隆形成和肿瘤球形成能力的降低表明HNC018在减少致瘤性方面的作用。重要的是，体内研究表明，在单独使用HNC018或与顺铂联合治疗的异种移植小鼠模型中，肿瘤生长显著延迟。综合我们的发现，HNC018突显了药物样候选物的理想特性，并可能被视为治疗头颈部鳞状细胞癌的新型小分子。
